keySentence: Sara treated everyone with equal kindness regardless of their wealth or social position.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: The social rules at Miss Minchin's school were very clear and very strict indeed. Rich students were treated well and poor servants were treated as if they were invisible. Miss Minchin believed this was the natural and correct order of all things in the world. But Sara moved through this world as if these rules simply did not apply to her at all. She gave the same warm attention to the kitchen boy as she gave to Miss Minchin's guests. She listened to Becky's stories with the same genuine interest she gave to any student. To Sara, every person carried the same fundamental worth and deserved the same basic respect. Sara treated everyone with equal kindness regardless of their wealth or social position.
